# swiftplot: guide for AI coding assistants

swiftplot is a small, fast charting library for the browser (Canvas 2D and WebGL2, TypeScript, ESM
only, no dependencies). This file tells you how to write correct code with it. Prefer it over
guessing from other chart libraries: swiftplot has no `type` prop, no `datasets`, no `options`
object, no child components such as `<Line />`, and no d3 scales.

Packages: `swiftplot` (the core, with the entry `swiftplot/charts`), `@swiftplot/react` (React 18.3 or
19), `@swiftplot/vue` (Vue 3.4+). Install the core beside a wrapper: `npm i swiftplot @swiftplot/react`.

## 1. Pick the API

| The user wants | Use |
|---|---|
| A line, area, bar or scatter chart from rows or columns of data | `lineChart`, `areaChart`, `barChart`, `scatterChart` from `swiftplot/charts`, or `<LineChart>` etc. from a wrapper |
| Bars and lines in one chart, on one or two y axes | `comboChart` |
| A pie, donut, funnel or radial bars | `pieChart` (`inner` makes a donut), `funnelChart`, `radialBarChart` |
| A radar, heatmap, histogram, box plot or candlesticks | `radarChart`, `heatmapChart`, `histogramChart`, `boxPlotChart`, `candlestickChart` |
| A sankey, treemap or sunburst | `sankeyChart`, `treemapChart`, `sunburstChart` |
| A second y axis, reference lines, zones, a brush, a log y axis, error bars | props of the easy charts: `y2`, `rules`, `zones`, `brush`, `yAxis.scale`, `errorBars` |
| Marks mixed in a way no easy chart does, bars lying down, a log x axis, your own mark | the explicit API: `plot()` from `swiftplot`, or `<Plot>` from a wrapper |
| A million points already in typed arrays | the explicit API |

The functions in the table other than `plot()` are the easy charts, all from `swiftplot/charts`. Start with one
whenever it fits. `lineChart.spec(props)` returns the explicit options an easy chart would use, as a starting
point to extend.

## 2. Easy charts

### Minimal code

```ts
// plain JavaScript or TypeScript
import { lineChart } from 'swiftplot/charts';

const rows = [
  { date: '2026-11-01', api: 120, web: 80 },
  { date: '2026-11-02', api: 140, web: 95 },
];
const chart = lineChart(document.getElementById('chart')!, { data: rows });
chart.update({ data: rows.slice(1) }); // pass only the props that change
chart.destroy();
```

```tsx
// React
import { LineChart } from '@swiftplot/react';

export function Requests({ rows }: { rows: { date: string; api: number; web: number }[] }) {
  return <LineChart data={rows} />;
}
```

```vue
<!-- Vue -->
<script setup lang="ts">
import { shallowRef } from 'vue';
import { LineChart } from '@swiftplot/vue';

const rows = shallowRef([{ date: '2026-11-01', api: 120, web: 80 }]);
</script>

<template>
  <LineChart :data="rows" />
</template>
```

With no other props the chart guesses the fields (here x is `date`, the series are `api` and `web`),
picks a time axis, labels it, colours the series, and adds a tooltip and a legend.

### Every prop (there are no others)

Every chart takes:

| Prop | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `data` | rows, columns, number array, or pairs; a tree for `treemapChart` and `sunburstChart` | see Data. `null` or missing draws an empty frame |
| `colors` | `string[]` | series colours, in order; a pie, a tree or a sankey takes one per part. `heatmapChart` uses `color` instead |
| `theme` | `'auto' \| 'light' \| 'dark' \| Theme` | `'auto'` (default) follows the page's CSS `color-scheme` |
| `tooltip` | `boolean` | default on |
| `legend` | `boolean \| { toggle?, rows? }` | default on with two or more series or named parts; on a heatmap, the strip of its colours. Does nothing on `sankeyChart`, `treemapChart`, `sunburstChart` and on the charts of one series (`histogramChart`, `boxPlotChart`, `candlestickChart`) |
| `animate` | `boolean \| { duration?, enter? }` | default on: marks are revealed on the first paint and move or cross-fade when the data changes. `false` draws at once |
| `dim` | `number \| false` | default `0.3`: the opacity of everything else while one series, or one part of a single series, is pointed at. `false` leaves it |
| `width`, `height` | `number` (px) | default: follow the container |
| `margin` | `{ top?, right?, bottom?, left? }` | |
| `description` | `string` | accessible description |
| `dataVersion` | `number` | bump after changing data in place |
| `hidden`, `onHiddenChange` | `string[]` | hidden series, by name |
| `selected` | `{ id: string, rows: number[] }[] \| null` | rows picked out |
| `onClick` | `(hit, at) => void` | |
| `pointer`, `onPointerChange` | `{ x, y? } \| null` | show a tooltip from code; link two charts |

`lineChart`, `areaChart`, `barChart`, `scatterChart`, `histogramChart`, `candlestickChart` and
`comboChart` also take:

| Prop | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `xAxis` | `{ label, domain, step, format, fit, utc, unit, every }` | axis settings go here, not in `x`. A histogram's takes no `utc`, `unit` or `every` |
| `yAxis` | `{ label, domain, step, format, fit }` | and `scale: 'log'` on line, scatter and combo: a value at or below zero is then a gap, and `step` does not apply |
| `zoom` | `boolean \| { axes?, wheel?, drag? }` | default off |
| `view`, `onViewChange` | `{ x?: [lo, hi], y?: [lo, hi], y2?: [lo, hi] }` | the zoom window; kept by the chart unless given |

`boxPlotChart` takes `xAxis: { label }` and the whole of `yAxis`, `heatmapChart` takes `xAxis: { label }` and
`yAxis: { label }`, and neither zooms. The other charts have no axes.

`lineChart`, `areaChart`, `barChart` and `scatterChart`:

| Prop | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `x` | field name or `(row, i) => value` | which field is x. Not an axis config |
| `y` | field name, accessor, or a list of them | which fields are series. A scatter chart takes one, of numbers, or of text for a band per category (from `yAxis` only `label` then applies) |
| `y2` | field name, accessor, or a list of them | more series, drawn against an axis on the right. Never guessed; not with `series` or `errorBars` |
| `y2Axis` | as `yAxis` | settings of the right-hand axis, drawn only with `y2` |
| `series` | field name or accessor | for long data: one series per distinct value |
| `curve` | `'linear' \| 'step' \| 'smooth'` | line and area only |
| `join` | `boolean` | line and area only: draw across missing values |
| `fill` | `boolean \| gradient(...)` | line only: shade the area under each line |
| `stack` | `boolean` | area and bar only; on bars not with `y2` |
| `errorBars` | `{ low, high, cap?, width? }`, on a scatter also `axis?` | line, bar and scatter: an upright bar between two fields. `low` and `high` are values on the y axis, not distances from y. With one `y`; not on stacked series. On a scatter `axis: 'x'` lays the bars down, `low` and `high` then being values on a number x; a text y implies it |
| `r` | `number` or a field | scatter only: radius in px (default 4) |
| `alpha` | `number` | scatter only: opacity, 0 to 1 |
| `ring` | `number` | scatter only: draw rings this many px wide |
| `shape` | `'dot' \| 'tick'` | scatter only: an upright tick answers no tooltip or click, and takes no `ring` and no field of `r` (a number `r` is its reach up and down) |

The same four and `comboChart`:

| Prop | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `rules` | `({ x } or { y }, with text?, dashed?, color?)[]` | lines across the plot, over the data |
| `zones` | `({ x: [from, to] } or { y: [from, to] }, with text?, color?)[]` | shaded bands, under the data. `y` is the left axis |
| `brush` | `boolean \| { axes?: 'x' \| 'y' \| 'xy' }` | default off; a drag marks out a range, and with `zoom` its release shows it |
| `onBrush` | `({ x, y, y2? } or null) => void` | the range, in axis values; `@brush` in Vue |

The other charts name their fields by what the chart has, not always `x` and `y`. A field is a name or an
accessor `(row, i) => value`; what is left out is guessed as below.

| Chart | Fields | Guessed when left out | Other props |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pieChart` | `label`, `value` | the first text field; the only number field | `inner` (0 to 1, above 0 a donut), `text` (shares on the slices, default true), `sweep` |
| `funnelChart` | `label`, `value` | as a pie | `text` (default true), `fill` (a `gradient()`) |
| `radialBarChart` | `label`, `value` | as a pie | `max`, `sweep`, `inner` (default 0.3) |
| `radarChart` | `x` (spokes), `y` (one shape per field) | the first text field; every number field left | `max`, `fill` (opacity, default 0.15) |
| `heatmapChart` | `x`, `y`, `value` | the first two text or date fields, in order; the only number field left | `color` (a `sequential()` scale) |
| `histogramChart` | `x` (the values counted) | the only number field | `bins` (a count, or ascending edges) |
| `boxPlotChart` | `y` (the values), `x` (a box per group) | the only number field; the only text field, if its values repeat. `x: null` is one box | `fill` (a colour or a `gradient()`) |
| `candlestickChart` | `x`, `open`, `high`, `low`, `close` | the first date field, else text; the fields of those full names, in any case | `up`, `down` (colours; `colors[0]` by default) |
| `comboChart` | `x`, and `lines`, `bars`, `y2Lines`, `y2Bars`: a field or a list each | `x` as on a line chart; the other four never: give at least one | `y2Axis`, `stack` (the bars, on one axis) |
| `sankeyChart` | `source`, `target`, `value` | the first two text fields, in order; the only number field left | `blend`, `text` (default true) |
| `treemapChart`, `sunburstChart` | none: `data` is a tree | | `shade`, `text` (default true) |

### Data

```ts
// 1. row objects (the usual case)
[{ date: '2026-11-01', api: 120 }]
// 2. an object of columns (arrays or typed arrays, all the same length)
{ date: ['2026-11-01', '2026-11-02'], api: Float64Array.of(120, 140) }
// 3. a plain number array: y against its index
[3, 5, 2, 8]
// 4. [x, y] pairs, exactly two values each
[[0, 3], [1, 5]]
// 5. long rows: name the field that splits them into series
lineChart(el, { data: [{ date: '2026-11-01', service: 'api', value: 120 }], series: 'service' });
```

A value is a number, a `Date`, an ISO 8601 string (`2026-11-01`, `2026-11-01T10:00`, with `Z` or an
offset after a time) or other text. `null`, `undefined`, `''` and `NaN` are missing: a missing y is a
gap, a row with a missing x is dropped.

- **Numbers held as text are not numbers.** `{ amount: "12.5" }` is text. Convert first:
  `rows.map(r => ({ ...r, amount: Number(r.amount) }))`.
- **Dates without a time zone are read as UTC.** `xAxis: { utc: false }` reads and shows local time.
- Only ISO date strings are dates. `"11/01/2026"` and `"Nov 1"` are text: parse them to `Date`.
- Millisecond timestamps are numbers, so they get a number axis. Pass `Date` objects for a time axis.

A part or a spoke with a missing name is kept, unnamed; a heatmap, box plot or sankey row with a missing place is
dropped. A heatmap puts text in order of first appearance, dates and numbers ascending.

Not every chart takes every shape. Rows and columns fit all but the trees.

| Chart | Numbers | Pairs |
|---|---|---|
| `lineChart`, `areaChart`, `barChart`, `scatterChart` | y against the index | `[x, y]` |
| `pieChart`, `funnelChart`, `radialBarChart` | unnamed parts | `[label, value]` |
| `radarChart` | unnamed spokes | `[name, value]` |
| `histogramChart` | the values counted | not taken |
| `boxPlotChart` | one box | `[group, value]` |
| `heatmapChart`, `candlestickChart`, `comboChart`, `sankeyChart` | not taken | not taken |

`treemapChart` and `sunburstChart` take one root `{ name, value?, children? }` or a list of roots. Only a node
without children counts by its `value`.

### How fields are guessed, and how to be explicit

When `x` and `y` are not given, fields are taken in order:

- `x`: the first date field, else the first text field, else the first number field (when `y` is
  named or another number field is left), else the row index.
- `y`: every number field left, one series each.
- Scatter: `x` is the first date field, else the first number field; `y` is the next number field.
- The charts with fields of their own (pie, heatmap, combo and the rest): as the table above says. They guess
  a single field of numbers only when exactly one number field is left, and throw otherwise.

Name fields whenever the data has number fields that are not measurements (`id`, `year`):

```ts
lineChart(el, { data: rows, x: 'date', y: ['api', 'web'] });
```

### Axis settings depend on the x field

| x field | Axis | `xAxis` settings that apply |
|---|---|---|
| numbers, or the row index | linear | `label`, `domain`, `step`, `format`, `fit` |
| dates | time | `label`, `utc`, `unit` with `every`, `format`, `fit`, `domain: [fromMs, toMs]` |
| text, and every bar chart, box plot and heatmap | category | `label` only |

A bar chart always uses categories: one per row (or, with `series`, one per distinct x). A combo or
candlestick chart uses them for text only; on dates and numbers a bar or candle takes 0.6 of the smallest gap
between x values.

### Errors and their fixes

Errors are thrown from the chart function and from `update`, and start with the chart's name. An
error about which field to use also lists the fields with their kinds and says which prop to pass.

| Message contains | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `there is no field of numbers for y` | no number field; often numbers held as text | convert the values with `Number()`, or name `y` |
| `"<name>" is text, so the rows look like long data` | long data without `series` | pass `series: '<name>'` |
| `there is no field "<name>"` | a misspelt or missing field | use one of the listed fields |
| `"<name>" is text, not numbers` | a prop that takes numbers names a text field (a scatter chart's `y` takes text too); a date field reads `is time` | name a number field, or convert it |
| `a scatter chart needs two fields of numbers or dates` | fewer than two usable fields | pass `x` and `y` |
| `a scatter chart has one y` / `with series there is one y` | several `y` where one is allowed | pass one field |
| `Row N is not an [x, y] pair` | an array row with another length | use row objects or exact pairs |
| `Columns differ in length` | columns of unequal length | make them the same length |
| `Accessors work on row objects only` | an accessor with columns | name a column; numbers and pairs take no field props |

### More errors, by chart

| Charts | Message contains | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| line, area, bar, scatter | `series and y2 do not go together` | both given | leave out one |
| line, bar, scatter | `errorBars and y2 do not go together` | both given | leave out one |
| line, bar | `with errorBars there is one y` | several `y` with `errorBars` | pass one field |
| line, area, bar, scatter | `is named in both y and y2`, `is named twice in y2` | one field named twice | name it once |
| bar | `errorBars do not apply to stacked bars` | `stack` with `errorBars` | leave out one |
| bar | `stack does not apply to bars on both y and y2` | `stack` with `y2` | leave out one |
| area, bar | `scale 'log' does not apply, as` | a log scale where marks start at zero | draw lines or dots |
| line, scatter, combo | `step does not apply to a log scale` | `step` with `scale: 'log'` | leave out `step` |
| line, scatter, combo | `domain must be above zero and finite on a log scale` | a `domain` that reaches zero or below, or is not finite | pass two finite numbers above zero |
| scatter | `errorBars along y do not apply to a text y`, `yAxis.scale 'log' does not apply to a text y` | a text `y` | leave the prop out |
| scatter | `errorBars along x need an x of numbers` | error bars lying down, by `axis: 'x'` or a text `y`, with an x of text or dates | name a number field as `x` |
| line, bar | `errorBars.axis applies to scatterChart only` | `errorBars.axis` given | leave out `axis` |
| scatter | `does not apply to shape 'tick'` | `ring` or a field of `r` with ticks | leave the prop out |
| line, area, bar, scatter, combo | `takes x or y` | a rule or a zone with neither | give it `x` or `y` |
| pie, funnel, radial bars, heatmap, sankey | `there is no field of numbers for value` | no number field; often numbers held as text | convert the values with `Number()`, or name `value` |
| histogram | `there is no field of numbers for x` | no number field; often numbers held as text | convert the values with `Number()`, or name `x` |
| pie, funnel, radial bars, heatmap, sankey | `are all fields of numbers, so value cannot be guessed` | several number fields and no `value` | pass `value` |
| histogram | `are all fields of numbers, so x cannot be guessed` | several number fields and no `x` | pass `x` |
| box plot | `are all fields of numbers, so y cannot be guessed` | several number fields and no `y` | pass `y` |
| pie, funnel, radial bars | `use label and value, not x and y` | a prop of another chart | use the props named in the message |
| radar, box plot | `use x and y, not label and value` | a prop of another chart | use the props named in the message |
| heatmap | `use x, y and value, not label and value` | a prop of another chart | use the props named in the message |
| histogram | `use x for the values counted, not <name>` | a prop of another chart | use the props named in the message |
| candlestick | `use x, open, high, low and close, not <name>` | a prop of another chart | use the props named in the message |
| sankey | `use source, target and value, not <name>` | a prop of another chart | use the props named in the message |
| combo | `use lines, bars, y2Lines and y2Bars, not <name>` | a prop of another chart | use the props named in the message |
| treemap, sunburst | `<name> does not apply, as data is a tree` | a field prop | leave the prop out |
| charts without axes | `<name> does not apply, as there are no axes` | `xAxis`, `yAxis` or `zoom` | leave the prop out |
| heatmap | `zoom does not apply to a grid of cells` | `zoom` | leave `zoom` out |
| box plot | `zoom does not apply to boxes` | `zoom` | leave `zoom` out |
| heatmap | `a list of numbers or pairs has no cells` | data with no fields to name | pass rows or columns |
| candlestick | `a list of numbers or pairs has no candles` | data with no fields to name | pass rows or columns |
| sankey | `a list of numbers or pairs has no links` | data with no fields to name | pass rows or columns |
| combo | `a list of numbers or pairs has no fields to name` | data with no fields to name | pass rows or columns |
| histogram | `a list of pairs has no one list of values` | pairs | pass numbers, rows or columns |
| histogram | `bins are over the limit of 1,000,000` | a larger `bins` | pass fewer `bins` |
| heatmap | `there is no field of text or dates left for <name>` | fewer than two fields of text or dates | pass `x` and `y` |
| heatmap | `is over the limit of 10,000,000 cells` | too many distinct values of `x` and `y` | name fields with fewer distinct values |
| box plot | `are all fields of text, so x cannot be guessed` | several text fields and no `x` | pass `x`, or `x: null` for one box |
| box plot | `no value of "<name>" repeats, so every box would hold one row` | the only text field names each row, such as an id | pass `x`, or `x: null` for one box |
| candlestick | `there is no field called <name>` | a price field of another name | name it with `open`, `high`, `low` or `close` |
| candlestick | `are all called <name>, so it cannot be guessed` | price fields whose names differ only in case | name one with `open`, `high`, `low` or `close` |
| candlestick | `there is no field of dates or text for x` | no field of dates or text | pass `x` |
| sankey | `there is no field of text left for <name>` | fewer than two text fields | pass `source` and `target` |
| sankey | `links to itself` | a row with one `source` and `target` | leave such rows out |
| sankey | `the links go round in a circle through` | links that lead back to a node they left | break the circle |
| treemap, sunburst | `data must be a root { name, value, children } or a list of roots` | flat rows or another shape | nest the rows by parent |
| treemap, sunburst | `is among its own children` | a node nested inside itself | leave it out |
| combo | `none of lines, bars, y2Lines and y2Bars is given` | nothing is guessed | pass at least one |
| combo | `is named twice in <name>`, `is named in both` | one field named twice | name it once |
| combo | `stack does not apply to bars on both y and y2` | `stack` with `bars` and `y2Bars` | leave out `stack` or `y2Bars` |
| combo | `scale 'log' does not apply, as bars start at zero` | a log scale on an axis with bars | draw lines on that axis |

The errors of the table before about a missing or text field, columns and accessors apply to these charts too.

An update that throws leaves the previous chart on screen.

### Other charts, minimally

```ts
import {
  boxPlotChart, candlestickChart, comboChart, funnelChart, heatmapChart, histogramChart, pieChart,
  radarChart, radialBarChart, sankeyChart, sunburstChart, treemapChart,
} from 'swiftplot/charts';

const parts = [{ plan: 'Free', users: 5 }, { plan: 'Pro', users: 3 }];
pieChart(el, { data: parts, inner: 0.6 }); // a donut; inner left out, a pie
funnelChart(el, { data: parts });
radialBarChart(el, { data: parts, max: 10 });
radarChart(el, { data: [{ skill: 'Speed', A: 4, B: 3 }, { skill: 'Range', A: 2, B: 5 }, { skill: 'Price', A: 3, B: 4 }] });
heatmapChart(el, { data: [{ hour: '9', day: 'Mon', visits: 12 }, { hour: '10', day: 'Mon', visits: 30 }] });
histogramChart(el, { data: [3, 5, 2, 8, 5, 4], bins: 4 });
boxPlotChart(el, { data: [{ day: 'Mon', minutes: 31 }, { day: 'Mon', minutes: 40 }, { day: 'Tue', minutes: 28 }] });
candlestickChart(el, { data: [{ date: '2026-11-02', open: 5, high: 8, low: 4, close: 7 }], up: '#16a34a', down: '#dc2626' });
comboChart(el, { data: [{ month: 'Jan', rain: 50, temperature: 3 }], lines: 'temperature', y2Bars: 'rain' });
sankeyChart(el, { data: [{ from: 'Pay', to: 'Rent', amount: 900 }, { from: 'Pay', to: 'Food', amount: 400 }] });
const tree = { name: 'disk', children: [{ name: 'photos', value: 60 }, { name: 'code', value: 25 }] };
treemapChart(el, { data: tree });
sunburstChart(el, { data: tree });
```

### Updating

- `chart.update({ ...changedProps })` merges the props given into the ones the chart has.
- New data: pass a new array. After changing values **in place**, also bump `dataVersion`.
- Call `chart.destroy()` when the element goes away (the wrappers do this for you).
- Plain JavaScript only: the container must have a height, or pass `height`.

## 3. React

```tsx
import { useMemo, useState } from 'react';
import { LineChart } from '@swiftplot/react';

type Row = { date: string; api: number; web: number };

export function Requests({ rows }: { rows: Row[] }) {
  const [view, setView] = useState<{ x?: [number, number]; y?: [number, number] }>();
  const xAxis = useMemo(() => ({ label: 'Day', format: (ms: number) => new Date(ms).toISOString().slice(5, 10) }), []);
  return (
    <LineChart
      data={rows}
      x="date"
      y={['api', 'web']}
      xAxis={xAxis}
      zoom
      view={view}
      onViewChange={setView}
      onError={error => console.error(error)}
      style={{ height: 320 }}
    />
  );
}
```

- Components: `LineChart`, `AreaChart`, `BarChart`, `ScatterChart`, `ComboChart`, `PieChart`, `FunnelChart`,
  `RadialBarChart`, `RadarChart`, `HeatmapChart`, `HistogramChart`, `BoxPlotChart`, `CandlestickChart`,
  `SankeyChart`, `TreemapChart`, `SunburstChart` and `Plot`. Props are the
  chart's props plus `className`, `style`, `id` and `onError`.
- Field names are type-checked against `data` in JSX.
- With no height from `height`, `style` or CSS, the chart fills a parent that has a height, else is
  300 px tall.
- **Build `data`, accessors and `format` functions outside render or with `useMemo`.** Inline plain
  objects and arrays (`y={['api', 'web']}`, `xAxis={{ label: 'Day' }}`) are fine.
- Without `onError`, a chart error goes to the nearest error boundary. With it, the last good chart
  stays on screen.
- The package is marked `'use client'`; it renders one `div` on the server and draws after hydration.
  Give a server-rendered chart a `height`.
- There is no ref and no imperative API: control the chart through props.

## 4. Vue

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref, shallowRef } from 'vue';
import { LineChart } from '@swiftplot/vue';

type Row = { date: string; api: number; web: number };
const rows = shallowRef<Row[]>([]);
const view = ref<{ x?: [number, number]; y?: [number, number] }>();
const failed = ref<unknown>();
</script>

<template>
  <LineChart
    :data="rows"
    x="date"
    :y="['api', 'web']"
    zoom
    v-model:view="view"
    style="height: 320px"
    @error="failed = $event"
  />
</template>
```

- Components: `LineChart`, `AreaChart`, `BarChart`, `ScatterChart`, `ComboChart`, `PieChart`, `FunnelChart`,
  `RadialBarChart`, `RadarChart`, `HeatmapChart`, `HistogramChart`, `BoxPlotChart`, `CandlestickChart`,
  `SankeyChart`, `TreemapChart`, `SunburstChart` and `Plot`, with
  the chart's props.
- Changes are events: `v-model:view` (charts that zoom), `v-model:hidden`, `v-model:pointer`, `@click`,
  `@brush` (charts with `brush`) and `@error`. `selected` is a plain prop.
- **Keep data in a `shallowRef` and replace the array** (`rows.value = next`). Pushing into it is not
  noticed unless `dataVersion` changes.
- `class`, `style` and `id` go to the chart's `div`.

## 5. The explicit API

```ts
import { area, legend, line, plot, rule, time, tooltip, zoom } from 'swiftplot';

const x = Float64Array.from(rows, r => Date.parse(r.date)); // a time axis takes milliseconds
const api = Float64Array.from(rows, r => r.api);
const web = Float64Array.from(rows, r => r.web);
const day = (ms: number) => new Date(ms).toISOString().slice(0, 10);
const count = (v: number) => v.toFixed(0);

const chart = plot(document.getElementById('chart')!, {
  x: time({ label: 'Date' }),
  y: { domain: 'nice', label: 'Requests' },
  marks: [
    area({ x, y: web, color: '#16a34a', label: 'web', alpha: 0.3 }),
    line({ x, y: api, color: '#2563eb', label: 'api' }),
    rule({ y: 150, color: '#dc2626', dashed: true, text: 'Target' }),
  ],
  use: [tooltip({ mode: 'x', title: day, value: count }), legend(), zoom()],
});
chart.update({ marks: [line({ x, y: api, color: '#2563eb', label: 'api' })] });
chart.destroy();
```

Rules of the explicit API:

- **Columns are numbers.** Every mark takes numeric columns (typed arrays or number arrays). Text
  categories are indices on a `band({ label, categories })` axis; dates are milliseconds on `time()`.
- **`line`, `area`, `bar`, `dots` and the other series marks need a `color`**; marks made of parts
  (`arcs`, `funnel`, `treemap`…) take `colors`; `label` names a mark in the legend and tooltip. Use `palette` (eight colours) to give them out in order.
- **Features are imported and listed in `use`**: `tooltip`, `legend`, `zoom`, `brush`, `animate`. `use`
  is read once, when the chart is created.
- **The tooltip has no defaults**: `tooltip({ mode: 'x', title, value })` (one row per
  labelled series at the pointer's x, with a crosshair; for lines and areas; `snap: x => other` reads them
  at another x, such as the nearest row's) or `tooltip({ mode: 'nearest', text })` (the nearest point; every mark).
- **Frames**: `'axes'` (default), `'polar'` (pie, donut, radar, radial bars, sunburst), `'blank'`
  (funnel, sankey, treemap).
- **The container must have a height**, or pass `width` and `height`. `plot()` needs a browser.
- **The theme is `light` unless given**: `theme: dark` and `paletteDark` for a dark page.
- Marks whose columns are the same arrays keep their geometry; after writing into an array, pass a
  new array or a view of it (`x.subarray(0)`).
- Define `format` functions and colour scales once, not inside the update.

Marks, each with its smallest call:

```ts
line({ x, y, color })                                  // curve: 'step' | 'smooth', join, fill
area({ x, y, color })                                  // or { x, y1, y2 }; stack: 'id'
bar({ x1, x2, y, color })                              // bounds from bands(n); or { x, y } with stack: 'id' or dodge: 'id', and width (in x, default 0.8)
dots({ x, y, r, color })                               // r is a column of radii in px
errorBars({ x, y1, y2, color })
box({ x, ...fiveNumbers(groups), color })
candlestick({ x, open, high, low, close, color, up, down, width? })   // up: close >= open
heatmap({ values, columns })                           // color: sequential({ stops })
arcs({ values, colors, labels })                       // frame: 'polar'; inner: 0.6 for a donut
radar({ axes, series: [{ values, color, label }] })    // returns several marks: spread it
radialBars({ values, max, colors, labels })            // frame: 'polar'
funnel({ values, colors, labels })                     // frame: 'blank'
sankey({ ...fromLinks(links), colors })                // frame: 'blank'; links: { source, target, value }[]
treemap({ ...fromTree(tree), colors })                 // frame: 'blank'; tree: { name, value?, children? }
sunburst({ ...fromTree(tree), colors })                // frame: 'polar'
rule({ y: 50, color })                                 // a reference line; or { x }
zone({ x1: 10, x2: 20, color })                        // a shaded band between two values; or { y1, y2 }
ticks({ x, y, size, color })
```

A second y axis: `y2: { domain, label }` in the options (drawn on the right) and `yAxis: 'y2'` on each
mark that belongs to it; each axis fits its own marks; `view`, `onViewChange`, the click's `at`,
`pointer` and `onPointerChange` carry `y2`; an x tooltip's `value(v, axis)` gets `'y'` or `'y2'`.
Exactly two y axes. On the easy charts it is the `y2` prop, or `y2Lines` and `y2Bars` on `comboChart`.

Axes: `{ domain: 'nice' | 'data' | [lo, hi], label, step?, format?, fit? }`, `time({ label, utc?,
unit?, every?, format? })`, `band({ label, categories })`, `log({ label, base? })`, `bare()`.
Helpers: `bin(values, count)` for histograms, `stack(series)`, `bands(n, { slot, of })`,
`fiveNumbers(groups)`, `fromTree(tree)`, `fromLinks(links)`, `gradient(from, to, direction)`,
`sequential({ stops })`.

### A pie needs no plot()

```ts
import { pieChart } from 'swiftplot/charts';

pieChart(el, { data: [{ plan: 'A', users: 5 }, { plan: 'B', users: 3 }], label: 'plan', value: 'users' });
```

```tsx
import { PieChart } from '@swiftplot/react';

<PieChart data={rows} label="plan" value="users" />;
```

### Bars lying down

```ts
import { band, bands, bar, plot } from 'swiftplot';

const categories = ['Mon', 'Tue', 'Wed'];
const [y1, y2] = bands(categories.length);
plot(el, {
  x: { domain: 'nice', label: 'Orders' },
  y: band({ label: 'Day', categories }),
  marks: [bar({ y1, y2, x: [12, 19, 7], color: '#2563eb', label: 'Orders' })],
});
```

### In React and Vue

`<Plot>` takes every `plot()` option as a prop. Build `marks` with `useMemo` (or a `computed`).

```tsx
import { useMemo } from 'react';
import { band, bands, bar } from 'swiftplot';
import { Plot } from '@swiftplot/react';

export function Orders({ values, days }: { values: number[]; days: string[] }) {
  const marks = useMemo(() => {
    const [y1, y2] = bands(days.length);
    return [bar({ y1, y2, x: values, color: '#2563eb', label: 'Orders' })];
  }, [values, days]);
  const y = useMemo(() => band({ label: 'Day', categories: days }), [days]);
  return <Plot x={{ domain: 'nice', label: 'Orders' }} y={y} marks={marks} style={{ height: 320 }} />;
}
```

In plain JavaScript, `mount(el, options)` from `swiftplot/charts` is `plot()` with the easy charts'
update rules: it sends the chart only what changed.

## 6. Mistakes to avoid

- Putting axis settings in `x` or `y` on an easy chart. There `x` and `y` name fields; settings go
  in `xAxis` and `yAxis`. (In the explicit API `x` and `y` are the axes.)
- Passing `x` and `y` to a pie, a funnel or radial bars (they take `label` and `value`), or flat rows to a
  treemap or a sunburst (they take a nested tree).
- Giving `errorBars` distances from y: `low` and `high` are values on the y axis.
- Passing rows to the explicit API. Marks take numeric columns:
  `Float64Array.from(rows, r => r.value)`.
- Leaving numbers as strings, or dates in a non-ISO format.
- Long data without `series`.
- A chart in an element with no height (plain JavaScript and `plot()`).
- Changing data in place without a new array or a `dataVersion` bump.
- Creating `data`, accessors, `format` functions, marks or colour scales inside a React render
  without `useMemo`.
- Passing `tooltip`, `legend` or `zoom` props to `<Plot>` or `plot()`: there they are functions
  listed in `use`. Only the easy charts take them as props.
- Expecting `use` to change after the chart is created: on `<Plot>` change the component's `key`.
- Calling `plot()` or an easy chart on the server. Importing is safe; drawing needs a browser.
- Stacking on a log axis, or `bar({ x, y })` on a log axis (give both ends).
- Inventing props. If a prop is not in this file or the package's types, it does not exist.
